plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to double flowers on sturdy stems above deeply lobed green foliage. It is a beloved cottage garden staple and a long-lived plant that can thrive for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies are often hosted by ants, which feed on the sugary nectar of the buds; contrary to myth, the ants are not required for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching, thorny deciduous shrub with delicate five-petaled flowers that have a light sweet scent. After flowering it produces bright red rose hips rich in vitamin C.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (June to July)
plants.location: Hedgerows, woodland edges and scrubland across Europe, northwest Africa and western Asia
plants.funFact: During World War II, rose hips from the dog rose were collected in Britain to make vitamin C-rich syrup when citrus imports were scarce.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and dense spikes of tiny tubular flowers that attract bees and butterflies. It thrives in full sun and well-drained, poor soils.
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean region; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania and the northern United States
plants.funFact: The name lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', as the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath. In the Southern Hemisphere's cooler season, some regions see flowers earlier, while in the Northern Hemisphere warm regions like California and the Mediterranean the main bloom peaks around June.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted along streets in California, Mexico, Portugal, South Africa, Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas have been planted that the city is nicknamed 'Jacaranda City', and fallen blossoms form purple carpets on the streets.
